claims.text: Boron-free laser-clad AlCoCrFeNiMoTi coatings on Q235 steel have a relatively coarse microstructure.
Boron-free laser-clad AlCoCrFeNiMoTi coatings exhibit less consistent passive-film formation.
Adding boron during laser cladding promotes in situ formation of dispersed TiB2 particles.
In situ TiB2 particles refine the coating microstructure.
In situ TiB2 particles enhance the stability and adhesion of the passive oxide film.
TiB2 particles act as micro-reinforcements that improve wear resistance.
TiB2 particles stabilize the passive oxide film against mechanical removal during sliding.
Stabilization of the passive film against mechanical removal mitigates localized corrosion.
The combined reinforcement and passive-film stabilization mechanism governs coupled tribo-corrosion degradation.
A boron addition around 1 wt% will produce lower overall degradation than the boron-free baseline.
A boron addition around 1 wt% will reduce the wear rate relative to the boron-free baseline.
A boron addition around 1 wt% will reduce corrosion current density relative to the boron-free baseline.
Low boron additions will provide insufficient reinforcement and inferior tribo-corrosion performance relative to the optimum.
Excessive boron will cause defect formation and inferior tribo-corrosion performance relative to the optimum.
The predicted benefit should hold under moderate sliding loads in simulated marine conditions.
Extreme mechanical loads or highly aggressive chemical environments may overwhelm passive-film repassivation and eliminate the predicted benefit.
Coatings containing 0, 0.5, 1, and 1.5 wt% added boron will be compared under controlled tribo-corrosion conditions.
Failure of every tested boron level to improve both wear resistance and corrosion protection relative to the boron-free control would falsify the hypothesis.
